transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Arcadia CISO), Janelle Park (Arcadia Security), Ravi Singh (Arcadia Compliance)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, i'm alex from redwood, this is priya our solutions engineer, how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Michael Torres: doing well, thanks. busy week but excited to talk through security posture.
[00:18] Alex Chen: great, quick agenda, we wanted to understand arcadia's compliance constraints, sso and identity, data residency, and any network requirements, then share how redwood approaches those. sound good?
[00:28] Janelle Park: yep, that's perfect. to be clear, arcadia processes PHI-ish notes, so we need strict controls. we have to know where data lives and who can see inference logs.
[00:38] Priya Nair: totally understood. first, are you evaluating hosted api or thinking dedicated/private from the start?
[00:45] Ravi Singh: procurement prefers hosted for speed, but compliance is pushing for dedicated or private for patient data. so both are on the table.
[00:55] Alex Chen: okay makes sense. from a security artifacts perspective, we can share SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, and our pen test summary — i'll drop those after the call.
[01:08] Michael Torres: excellent. can you also include the scoping of those audits, like environment coverage? sometimes certs don't cover cloud provider managed layers.
[01:18] Priya Nair: yes i'll include the audit scope docs and a summary of what the control coverage looks like — e.g., control coverage for hosted control plane vs customer-managed private deployments.
[01:28] Janelle Park: on identity, we use SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning. we need role mappings and ability to enforce least privilege. how does redwood handle that?
[01:38] Priya Nair: we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; you can map SAML attributes to roles. our RBAC model supports tenancy-level roles: admin, developer, observer, plus custom roles.
[01:50] Ravi Singh: do you support enforced MFA from the IdP? we need to ensure there's no fallback that skips MFA.
[01:57] Priya Nair: enforcement is done at the IdP — redwood honors assertion from the IdP; we can require signed assertions and enforce session timeouts. we also support device-level attributes if needed.
[02:10] Michael Torres: good. what about audit logs — is every API call and token usage logged, and can we export logs to our SIEM?
[02:20] Alex Chen: yes, audit logs capture admin actions, model deploys, API key events, and user activity. for Hosted we stream logs to our secure log store and we can push logs to your SIEM via S3 delivery or syslog depending on the setup. for Dedicated/Private you control the log sink.
[02:38] Janelle Park: retention — our policy is 7 years for certain records, but for operational logs we keep 1-3 years. what's the retention for hosted?
[02:48] Priya Nair: default retention is 90 days on hosted tier; extended retention is available as an add-on (1yr/3yr) for enterprise customers. for dedicated/private you can set retention to match your policies.
[03:00] Ravi Singh: we also need immutable audit trails for some artifacts. does redwood support WORM or append-only mechanisms?
[03:08] Priya Nair: for hosted we provide tamper-evident log records and can integrate with your archival store that supports WORM. For private deployments you can configure append-only storage. i'll flag that as a follow-up to show the exact implementation.
[03:20] Michael Torres: encryption — at rest and in transit? what key management options do you offer?
[03:26] Alex Chen: in transit is TLS 1.2+/1.3. at rest we encrypt using AES-256. for hosted we manage keys by default, but enterprise customers can bring their own keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations — and for private deployments we support HSM-backed KMS as well.
[03:42] Janelle Park: BYOK sounds good. do you integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS?
[03:48] Priya Nair: yes, we have integrations for AWS KMS and KMS-backed HSM, Azure Key Vault is supported through our enterprise connector, and GCP KMS is on the roadmap — we'll confirm timelines in the note.
[04:00] Ravi Singh: on data lifecycle — inference inputs/output — what's retained, and how do you support deletion requests?
[04:08] Alex Chen: by default hosted logs and response caches are kept short — 30-90 days depending on config. we support data deletion APIs and a policy-driven automatic purge; for workloads requiring no retention we can operate with zero retention mode or dedicated private deployments where you control ephemeral caches.
[04:24] Michael Torres: we need proof that deletions are executed. do you provide deletion audit entries?
[04:30] Priya Nair: yes deletion events are logged with a tombstone entry and we can provide manifests of deleted keys/objects.
[04:36] Janelle Park: regarding network, for dedicated/private we need VPC peering and strict egress IPs for allowlisting. do you support that?
[04:45] Alex Chen: yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and static egress IP ranges; Private deployments can run inside your VPC on-prem. we also support IP allowlist and mutual TLS for service-to-service.
[04:58] Ravi Singh: any requirement for routing PCI/PHI traffic through your control plane? procurement asks if data ever transits outside customer networks.
[05:06] Priya Nair: for hosted API, inference requests hit our control plane and pass through our runtime in our cloud regions. for Private, you can run the runtime entirely inside your network and keep the control plane separated — there's a hybrid mode too. we'll detail network flow diagrams in the follow-up.
[05:22] Michael Torres: okay, please include a diagram. also, do you have SOC-level controls for third-party subprocessors? who are they?
[05:30] Alex Chen: yes we maintain a subprocessors list; common ones are cloud providers (AWS), logging/CDN providers. we'll provide the current list and subprocessors' attestations.
[05:40] Janelle Park: incident response — do you have an SLA for breach notifications and a runbook?
[05:46] Priya Nair: we have an incident response policy, typically 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches, and we can provide an executive summary of the runbook and contact process for enterprise contracts.
[05:58] Ravi Singh: are you SOC2 Type II reports available under NDA?
[06:02] Alex Chen: yes, we'll provide the full SOC2 report under an NDA. i'll send steps to sign the NDA and then share the artifacts.
[06:10] Michael Torres: great. on RBAC in the product, can we granularly control who can access model logs vs who can kick off inferences?
[06:18] Priya Nair: yes, we have fine-grained permissions — separation between runtime permissions (invoke model) and admin permissions (view logs, modify model). custom roles are supported.
[06:28] Janelle Park: how about service accounts for our applications — are there scoped API keys with narrow privileges?
[06:34] Priya Nair: scoped service tokens are supported; you can scope by model, route, and TTL. tokens can be rotated automatically and we log token activity.
[06:44] Michael Torres: token exposure is a big risk. do you offer automatic token rotation and immediate revocation?
[06:50] Priya Nair: yes, rotation and revocation are built-in and available via API. for Dedicated we can integrate rotation with your secret manager.
[06:58] Alex Chen: switching to compliance posture — any regulatory frameworks besides HIPAA you need to meet?
[07:04] Ravi Singh: HIPAA for sure, plus some state-level privacy regs and internal policies around data residency — certain datasets must remain in the us-east region.
[07:12] Priya Nair: we support region pinning for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private you control region entirely. we'll list available regions and whether certified controls apply per region.
[07:22] Michael Torres: can redwood provide a BAA?
[07:25] Alex Chen: yes, we offer a BAA for customers processing PHI — we'll share the standard template and we can negotiate terms as needed.
[07:34] Janelle Park: procurement might push back on cost for Dedicated. what are the typical throughput/latency tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated?
[07:42] Priya Nair: Hosted is fully managed and best for quick integration; Dedicated gives stronger isolation and predictable SLAs with reserved GPU capacity, lower tail latency for steady workloads. cost for Dedicated is higher but gives capacity guarantees. we can run a short benchmark PoC to quantify this.
[07:58] Michael Torres: a benchmark would help — especially around 99th percentile latency for our typical doc lengths.
[08:04] Alex Chen: we can run a benchmark; priya will work with you on sample payloads and sequence lengths.
[08:10] Ravi Singh: procurement will also ask for proof of encryption key custody — in other words, do you have access to keys if we BYOK?
[08:18] Priya Nair: with BYOK we don't hold the plaintext keys; we integrate with your KMS and key operations require your authorization. for some hosted options we can offer key escrow models under contract.
[08:30] Michael Torres: what about pen tests? do you give results or a summary?
[08:34] Alex Chen: we provide a summary and remediation plan; full reports can be shared under NDA.
[08:40] Janelle Park: can we get a sample of audit logs, like format and a sample event stream? that will speed up SIEM onboarding.
[08:48] Priya Nair: yes — i'll include a sanitized sample export (json) and a mapping for fields to your SIEM.
[08:56] Ravi Singh: any certifications around supply chain or software bill of materials?
[09:00] Alex Chen: we publish SBOMs for our runtime components and can share those under NDA.
[09:06] Michael Torres: ok that's good. a few quick clarifying questions — for zero retention mode, does that impact caching and therefore latency?
[09:15] Priya Nair: zero retention disables persistent prefix caches; we still do in-memory session caches for the duration of the request to preserve latency, but you lose cross-request prefix caching, which can increase tokens and cost slightly. we'll quantify this in the PoC.
[09:32] Janelle Park: for private deployments, what's the ops burden? do you manage upgrades?
[09:38] Alex Chen: for Private we offer two models: customer-managed with our distro (you run it) or managed private where we perform upgrades via a secure channel and follow a maintenance window. we'll outline responsibilities in the runbook.
[09:52] Ravi Singh: any SOC2 control gaps we should know about for hosted?
[09:57] Priya Nair: no major gaps; some customers ask for longer retention and additional regional attestations which we can add as enterprise features. we'll call out any residual exclusions in the SOC report.
[10:08] Michael Torres: ok that helps. can you also share your vulnerability disclosure program and contact?
[10:13] Alex Chen: yes we'll include our VDP and contact email.
[10:18] Janelle Park: is there an SLA for forensic support? if we need logs for an audit, how quickly can you pull them?
[10:25] Priya Nair: for enterprise customers we include a certain number of forensic hours in the contract and can pull requested logs within an agreed SLA — typically 48-72 hours.
[10:36] Ravi Singh: good. one more from legal — subprocessors' sub-subprocessors? procurement asks how deep you track.
[10:43] Alex Chen: we maintain a list and can provide details upon request. deeper chains are tracked where we rely on suppliers for security controls.
[10:50] Michael Torres: alright, that's most of our security checklist. next steps?
[10:55] Alex Chen: recap — i'll send SOC2/ISO and BAA template; priya will share SSO/SCIM, RBAC docs, audit log samples, and a network diagram. we'll propose dates for a Dedicated/Private deep-dive and a performance PoC.
[11:08] Janelle Park: sounds good. Ravi, michael, any other asks?
[11:12] Ravi Singh: please include cost ballparks for Dedicated and the enterprise add-ons (log retention, BYOK, extended SLAs).
[11:20] Michael Torres: and include region availability and whether those controls apply regionally.
[11:26] Alex Chen: will do. we'll follow up by email with artifacts and a calendar invite. thanks everyone for your time.
[11:34] Janelle Park: thanks, appreciate it.
[51:30] (call ends)
